_comment: Build-time feature gates. Edit and rebuild to change. allow_delete_user exposes the destructive 'delete_user.sh' entry in the Scripts menu; keep it false unless the build is intended for admins who need it. primary_bastion_filter / secondary_bastion_filter narrow the Scripts dialog bastion dropdowns to instances whose name or id contains the given text (case-insensitive); empty shows all. protected_users are never deleted by delete_user (case-insensitive); the script also hardcodes system-account protection as a backstop.
_alerts_comment: On-call Alerts button (Jira Service Management Operations). cloud_id + email identify the JSM site to query. allowed_users lists the OS usernames (Windows USERNAME / Linux USER, matched case-insensitively) that may see the Alerts button; use ["*"] for everyone, [] to hide it from everyone. The button only appears when cloud_id AND email are set AND the user is on the list. DO NOT commit a real API token in 'token' — this file is in git. Leave it empty and have each user set JIRA_TOKEN in their environment; JIRA_TOKEN always overrides this value.
_personal_scripts_comment: "Add Script" in the Scripts menu (save your own shell scripts, optionally bound to a hotkey, that paste into the focused connection tab) is available to everyone. This section instead gates the git integration: users on allowed_users are prompted once for a git personal access token, get git's credential store on the remote box populated by Prep Terminal (scoped to git_host, so git clone/pull over HTTPS just work), and receive the hardcoded default_scripts below (e.g. a Ctrl+1 're-clone the repo' script). Users NOT on the list can still create their own scripts and bind Ctrl+1 themselves. Matching: OS username, case-insensitive, ["*"] = everyone, [] = nobody (the shipped default). The PAT is cached in the user's local config.ini (base64, not encrypted) — never in this file. default_scripts fields: name, hotkey (e.g. "Ctrl+1"), body (the shell script; the credential store makes the clone auth automatically). In a body, {{user}} is replaced with the local OS username (the allowed_users name) before it runs — use it for per-user paths like /home/efs/{{user}}, since the remote $USER is the SSM/root account, not the person running the app.
